title: Three rules collapse to one — present Roman Church judgment alone discerns
source_text: XIX. Sed rursus hae tres regulae in unicam contrahi possunt, hanc nempe, Quod quicquid Ecclesia Romana tanquam divinam aut Apostolicam traditionem proponit, pro traditione tali indubitato sit habendum. Quemadmodum enim Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae authoritatem librorum diu notorum quoad nos ab Ecclesiae praesentis testimonio suspendunt, ita quoque nonnisi ejusdem judicio traditiones veras a falsis certo & infallibiliter discerni & distingui volunt.
pass_a_gloss: But again these three rules can be drawn together into one, namely this: that whatever the Roman Church proposes as a divine or Apostolic tradition is without doubt to be held as such a tradition. For just as the doctors of the Roman Church hang the authority of books long known, as far as we are concerned, on the testimony of the present Church, so also they will have true traditions discerned and distinguished from false ones certainly and infallibly only by that same judgment.
pass_b_english: The three rules fold into one: whatever Rome proposes as Divine or Apostolic tradition must be taken as such without doubt.

As they hang the authority of long-known books on the present Church's witness, so they will have true traditions sorted from false ones only by that same judgment — and that with certainty and infallibility.

choices.why: Removes private testing of tradition claims.
Canonical authority deferred to present Church testimony.
